subject: Novexa: scoped retention evidence request and sample proof-of-delete
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novexa.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: privacy@novexa.com
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Retention evidence request — EU tenant (SOC 2 / SIG follow-up)

Hi Neha / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our security team asked for a scoped delivery of retention and deletion evidence specifically for our EU tenant (Novexa Health). The asks are:

- A mapping of what categories of logs are retained (session traces, ephemeral inference caches, system audit logs) and the default TTLs by category.
- The process and artifacts you produce when a customer requests targeted deletion (proof-of-delete manifest, timestamps, keystore rotation notes).
- Any customer-specific exceptions or carveouts you support (e.g., short-term forensic holds, extended retention for legal holds).

I've attached our SOC2/SIG questionnaire extract with the specific questions highlighted (Novexa_SOC2_Questions_v1.pdf). Can you confirm whether you can provide a sample evidence packet (anonymized) showing a proof-of-delete for ephemeral inference logs and the retention matrix for our tenant?

We'd like to include a signed attestation if possible. Target deadline for internal review is Nov 8 — is that feasible?

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Security Program Manager — Novexa Health
elena.ruiz@novexa.com

---
Attachment: Novexa_SOC2_Questions_v1.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novexa.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention evidence request — EU tenant (SOC 2 / SIG follow-up)

Hi Elena — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks.

Short answers up front: yes, we can provide an anonymized sample proof-of-delete packet for ephemeral inference logs, and we can also provide the tenant-scoped retention matrix for the EU region. We can include a short signed attestation that covers the artifacts we deliver.

Couple of clarifying points so we scope the packet correctly:

- Do you need a sample that includes exported keystore rotation metadata (key IDs / rotation timestamps), or is redaction of key identifiers ok as long as rotation timestamps and KMS audit references are included?
- For the proof-of-delete, are you expecting a single-tenant deletion event (one set of session traces) or a small batch (5–10 manifests) to demonstrate the workflow?
- For legal holds: do you have an active case id or internal hold id we should reference in the attestation? We can show both the standard process and an example of a temporary forensic hold workflow.

Proposed timeline:
- EOD Oct 29 — we share the retention matrix (spreadsheet) and a short process note.
- Nov 1 — we deliver anonymized sample proof-of-delete + manifest and draft attestation for your review.

I've attached our internal retention matrix template (redwood_retention_matrix.xlsx) so you can confirm the columns you want populated. If that timeline works I'll coordinate with Ben on producing the sample manifests.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security & Risk Analyst | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

---
Attachment: redwood_retention_matrix.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novexa.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention evidence request — EU tenant (SOC 2 / SIG follow-up)

Elena / team,

Adding a few technical details so you have visibility into the artifacts we'll include in the sample packet:

- Ephemeral inference logs: We retain request/response traces for debugging for a default of 7 days for ephemeral sessions in the EU region; these are stored in tenant-scoped blobs and indexed in our ephemeral trace service. For SOC 2 evidence we can provide:
  - A sample delete manifest (JSON) that includes tenant id (anonymized), object keys deleted, deletion timestamps (UTC), and the deletion job id.
  - System audit entry showing the delete job invocation and operator/service account that executed the workflow.

- Keystore rotation: We do not disclose raw key material. The evidence packet will include rotation timestamps, KMS key aliases (redacted), and the KMS audit reference IDs which you can use to validate via your KMS link.

- For hold workflows: we will demonstrate a short-term forensic hold example. The example will show: hold creation timestamp, the internal hold id, affected object patterns, and the process to lift the hold.

- Sampling approach: rather than 10 full manifests, proposing 3 representative manifests covering (1) single-tenant delete, (2) bulk purge with prefix match, (3) hold-lift event. This keeps the deliverable compact but demonstrates the full lifecycle.

I've uploaded the draft artifacts to the shared folder: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/novexa-evidence-poc (read-only).

Let me know if Elena wants additional columns in the retention matrix or a walkthrough call next week.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Compliance Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

---
Related link: JIRA-SEC-2345
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novexa.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, privacy@novexa.com
Date: 2026-11-02T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Retention evidence request — EU tenant (SOC 2 / SIG follow-up)

Thanks — that approach looks good. A few final asks before you produce the sample packet: 

- Please redact tenant identifiers but keep a stable pseudonym (e.g., "novexa-tenant-1") so we can match artifacts across manifests.
- Include the signed attestation text as a separate PDF (we can accept an electronic signature). The attestation should reference the artifacts by filename and include a statement that the artifacts reflect Redwood's production retention and deletion workflows as of the artifact timestamps.
- For the keystore rotation references, redaction of aliases is fine as long as the rotation timestamps and KMS audit IDs are present.

If you can deliver the packet by Nov 5 EOD (UTC) we'll hit our internal review cadence. If anything slips, please flag no later than Nov 3 so we can adjust.

Happy to take a quick 30-minute call if helpful — otherwise we'll review the Drive artifacts and get back.

Best,
Elena

Attachment requested: novexa_sample_proof_manifest.pdf
